City level: The phrasing “Hochschule für Musik und Tanz” is the formal name of the music and dance university in Köln (Cologne). Other major German cities use different institution names (e.g., München and Hamburg use “…Musik und Theater,” Düsseldorf is “Robert Schumann Hochschule”). The waterfront promenade with Rhine-style stairs and metal bollards suggests the Rhine riverfront typical of Cologne’s Altstadt-Nord area.
Street level: The photo shows a short street that terminates directly at a building signed “HOCHSCHULE FÜR MUSIK UND TANZ,” with angled parking on the right and a Rhine promenade with stair access on the left. This matches the main HfMT Köln building situated just off the Rhine embankment near Unter Krahnenbäumen, where cross streets lead perpendicularly from the river promenade to institutional buildings. The distinctive riverside bollards and stair modules, combined with the facade signage of the institution, narrow it to the block around the HfMT main building.
Elimination: Other German Rhine cities with river promenades (Düsseldorf, Bonn, Mainz) lack an institution with exactly this name; likewise, the architecture and dense Altstadt block pattern align well with Cologne rather than the others.
